item.title: A South Bay Mystery: What Happened to All the Tree Frogs?
item.description: Both locally in California and around the world, numbers of amphibians are on the decline.

item.title: New Poll Finds Race for California Governor Remains Deadlocked
item.description: Former Rep. Katie Porter, Rep. Eric Swalwell, investor Tom Steyer, commentator Steve Hilton and Riverside County Sheriff Chad Bianco remain closely divided in a new Public Policy Institute of California survey.

item.title: California Democrats Leave Governor’s Race Unsettled as Gaza Fight Looms
item.description: At their San Francisco convention, California Democrats failed to endorse a gubernatorial candidate and wrestled with deep divisions over Israel’s war in Gaza, signaling a fractured party heading into the June primary.

item.title: Riverside County Case Highlights Accountability for Federal Immigration Agents
item.description: A Temecula man was charged after allegedly impersonating a federal immigration officer and threatening a 17-year-old, shining a spotlight on the limits of accountability for federal agents — a debate echoing across California.

item.title: BART Service Resumes After Network Failure Disrupts Morning Commute
item.description: The meltdown is the second service disruption this week, and the latest in a series of major incidents affecting transit riders.

item.title: San Francisco Court Clerks Launch Strike Over Staffing and Criminal Case Backlogs
item.description: The union said staffing has been spread thin for years, but that the high volume of cases filed by District Attorney Brooke Jenkins’ office has exacerbated the problem.

item.title: Misinformation Leads to Confusion in Fresno’s Immigrant Communities
item.description: Central Valley authorities have not said whether federal immigration agents have ramped up their presence in the area.

item.title: Judge Says California Must Allow 20,000 Immigrant Drivers to Reapply for Commercial Licenses
item.description: Under pressure from the Trump administration, California planned to revoke the licenses next week. A state court’s ruling, expected in the coming days, will likely offer drivers a way to keep their licenses.

item.title: Potential Oakland Teachers Strike: What Should Families Know?
item.description: Oakland Unified School District educators voted to authorize a strike last week, following a year of labor negotiations with no deal.

item.title: Xavier Becerra on Why His Upbringing and Career Give Him an Edge Over Other Gubernatorial Candidates
item.description: First Latino Health Secretary Xavier Becerra says his working class upbringing and career in public service makes him the best candidate for governor of California.
